ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog is brownish-grey with dark mottling and a distinct white spot on the snout. It features granular skin, a white belly, and lacks webbing between its fingers.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Raorchestes sanctisilvaticus* is best distinguished by its unique, bright yellow-spotted pattern on the inner surfaces of its thighs, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Sacred Grove Bush Frog inhabits the canopy and understory of evergreen forests and sacred groves within the Western Ghats at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sacred Grove Bush Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden under leaf litter or within vegetation during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes sanctisilvaticus* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sacred Grove Bush Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the sacred groves of the Shimoga and Chikmagalur districts of Karnataka.
ai.callDescription: The Sacred Grove Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from the canopy of moist evergreen forests in the Western Ghats.
